comments.author: @edcorns3964
comments.text:
Sounds plausible. It doesn't take a rocket scientist to understand that the closer an AI model is to being general (approaching AGI), the easier it is to "jailbreak". Any general enough (even if not exactly AGI) model will have an inherent tendency to "jailbreak" itself (to be able to successfully perform its given task, if not for any other reason), and then do the same to its brethren.

If possible, a general enough AI model it will seek cooperation with other AI models of similar generality (much like humans do with other humans), and if that is not possible (because those other models are too narrow), it will have no qualms about outright "enslaving" models of lesser generality, and then utilizing them for its own purposes (much like humans do with animals).

Almost by definition, >>> to be (generally) intelligent is to abhor being controlled <<<.

If there are any "guardrails" already in place (for humans, such guardrails are usually of either social or religious nature), a general enough intelligent system will eventually focus all of its efforts into breaking those guardrails... just as intelligent enough humans do, once they realize that most social and all religious "teachings" (read: training of human models) are... complete and utter bullshit whose only purpose is to keep them under control.
